title: Why some people are always late
titleChinese: 一些人约会总是迟到的原因
paragraphs: We all have that one friend who is always late, don‘t we? The one who turns up half an hour after the appointed coffee time. The person who is seemingly perpetually ‘stuck in traffic‘. This dear friend will send a message saying “sorry, a bit delayed” when they’re already 20 minutes behind schedule. I mean, what kind of friend is that? Or, if you‘re really honest, is that persistently tardy person actually you?
Either way, if you’re on the receiving end, lateness can be extremely irritating, even infuriating. How on earth can people be so inconsiderate?

Well, recent research suggests that there might be more to this than simple rudeness. Psychologists from Washington University believe people perceive time differently. Their study gave participants a specific amount of time in which to complete a task, and even provided them with a clock. Despite this, some people became so engrossed in the activity that they completely lost track of time and forgot to check the clock.

According to psychologist Dr Susan Krauss Whitborne, from University of Massachusetts Amherst, this is like when we scroll through our social media feed and think only five minutes have elapsed, when in fact twenty have slipped by. Does that feel familiar? She writes in Psychology Today that those who were better at clock-checking were therefore “less reliant on their potentially flawed internal timekeeper.” So, what about the reasons beyond our faulty inner clocks?

Well, our personality also plays a role. Laura Clarke writes for BBC Capital that the less punctual among us often share traits such as “optimism, low levels of self-control, anxiety, or a penchant for thrill-seeking”. Why optimism, you ask? Optimists tend to overestimate how much they can achieve and underestimate problems — which means they don‘t account for the long traffic jam on the way to meet you for that coffee.

Here’s another thought: maybe language is to blame? The English phrase ‘to be fashionably late‘ is used to describe the optimum time to arrive at an event. If you’re too early, you can appear overly eager, but if you‘re a bit late you seem cool and sophisticated. The problem is, what one person regards as fashionably late, another may view as plain impolite. So, next time you have coffee, do try to be on time.

vocabulary.entry: appointed [adj.] /əˈpɔɪntɪd/ 指定的；约定的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: We met at the appointed time and place.
vocabulary.translation: 我们在约定的时间和地点见面了。

vocabulary.entry: persistently [adv.] /pəˈsɪstəntli/ 持续地；坚持不懈地
vocabulary.example: He persistently asked questions throughout the lecture.
vocabulary.translation: 整个讲座期间他不停地提问。

vocabulary.entry: infuriating [adj.] /ɪnˈfjʊərieɪtɪŋ/ 令人怒不可遏的；使人极为生气的
vocabulary.example: His constant lateness is infuriating.
vocabulary.translation: 他老是迟到，真让人恼火。

vocabulary.entry: perceive [v.] /pəˈsiːv/ 感知；认为 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: How do you perceive the current situation?
vocabulary.translation: 你如何看待当前的情况？

vocabulary.entry: engrossed in [phr.] /ɪnˈɡrəʊst ɪn/ 全神贯注于；专心致志于
vocabulary.example: She was engrossed in her book and didn‘t hear me.
vocabulary.translation: 她全神贯注地看书，没听见我说话。

vocabulary.entry: elapsed [v.] /ɪˈlæpst/ （时间）流逝；过去 (原形: elapse；书面语)
vocabulary.example: Several years elapsed before they met again.
vocabulary.translation: 几年过去了他们才再次见面。

vocabulary.entry: flawed [adj.] /flɔːd/ 有缺陷的；有瑕疵的
vocabulary.example: The plan is flawed and needs revision.
vocabulary.translation: 这个计划有缺陷，需要修改。

vocabulary.entry: penchant for [phr.] /ˈpentʃənt fɔː/ 对……的嗜好；偏爱 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: She has a penchant for expensive handbags.
vocabulary.translation: 她偏爱昂贵的手袋。

vocabulary.entry: tardy [adj.] /ˈtɑːdi/ 迟到的；拖延的 (正式用语)
vocabulary.example: He was tardy for the third time this week.
vocabulary.translation: 这是他本周第三次迟到了。

vocabulary.entry: inconsiderate [adj.] /ˌɪnkənˈsɪdərət/ 不体贴的；不替别人着想的
vocabulary.example: It was inconsiderate of him to play loud music at night.
vocabulary.translation: 他晚上大声播放音乐真是不体谅人。

vocabulary.entry: scroll [v.] /skrəʊl/ 滚动；滚动查看
vocabulary.example: She scrolled through her phone looking for the message.
vocabulary.translation: 她滚动手机查找那条消息。

vocabulary.entry: feed [n.] /fiːd/ 消息动态；信息流 (社交媒体术语)
vocabulary.example: My social media feed is full of holiday photos.
vocabulary.translation: 我的社交媒体动态里满是度假照片。

vocabulary.entry: reliant [adj.] /rɪˈlaɪənt/ 依赖的；依靠的
vocabulary.example: The country is heavily reliant on oil imports.
vocabulary.translation: 这个国家严重依赖石油进口。

vocabulary.entry: internal [adj.] /ɪnˈtɜːnəl/ 内部的；体内的
vocabulary.example: The body has an internal clock that regulates sleep.
vocabulary.translation: 身体有一个调节睡眠的内在生物钟。

vocabulary.entry: punctual [adj.] /ˈpʌŋktʃuəl/ 准时的；守时的
vocabulary.example: Please try to be punctual for the meeting.
vocabulary.translation: 请尽量准时参加会议。

vocabulary.entry: optimism [n.] /ˈɒptɪmɪzəm/ 乐观；乐观主义
vocabulary.example: Despite the difficulties, he maintained his optimism.
vocabulary.translation: 尽管困难重重，他仍然保持乐观。

vocabulary.entry: underestimate [v.] /ˌʌndərˈestɪmeɪt/ 低估；对……估计不足
vocabulary.example: Never underestimate the power of a kind word.
vocabulary.translation: 永远不要低估一句好话的力量。

vocabulary.entry: account for [phr.] /əˈkaʊnt fɔː/ 解释；说明
vocabulary.example: Can you account for your absence yesterday?
vocabulary.translation: 你能解释一下你昨天缺席的原因吗？

vocabulary.entry: sophisticated [adj.] /səˈfɪstɪkeɪtɪd/ 世故的；有品位的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: He has a sophisticated taste in wine.
vocabulary.translation: 他对葡萄酒有高雅的品味。

vocabulary.entry: plain [adv.] /pleɪn/ 简直；绝对地 (口语；用于强调)
vocabulary.example: That is just plain wrong.
vocabulary.translation: 那简直是完全错误的。

sentences.chinese: 或者，如果你真的坦诚的话，这个一直迟到的人实际上就是你自己呢？

sentences.english: How on earth can people be so inconsiderate?
sentences.chinese: 这些人到底怎么能如此不顾及别人呢？

sentences.english: Well, recent research suggests that there might be more to this than simple rudeness.
sentences.chinese: 嗯，最近的研究表明，这件事可能不仅仅是无礼那么简单。

sentences.chinese: 华盛顿大学的心理学家们认为人们对时间的感知是不同的。

sentences.chinese: 他们的研究给参与者规定了完成一项任务的特定时间，甚至还给他们提供了一个时钟。

sentences.english: Despite this, some people became so engrossed in the activity that they completely lost track of time and forgot to check the clock.

sentences.chinese: 根据马萨诸塞大学阿默斯特分校的心理学家苏珊·克劳斯·惠特伯恩博士的说法，这就好比我们浏览社交媒体的消息动态时，以为只过去了五分钟，而实际上不知不觉已经过去了二十分钟。

sentences.english: Does that feel familiar?
sentences.chinese: 这种感觉熟悉吗？

sentences.english: She writes in Psychology Today that those who were better at clock-checking were therefore “less reliant on their potentially flawed internal timekeeper.”
sentences.chinese: 她在《今日心理学》上写道，那些更善于看钟的人因此“更少依赖他们潜在有缺陷的内在时间感知机制”。

sentences.english: So, what about the reasons beyond our faulty inner clocks?
sentences.chinese: 那么，除了我们有缺陷的内在时钟之外，还有哪些原因呢？

sentences.english: Well, our personality also plays a role.
sentences.chinese: 嗯，我们的性格也起到一定作用。

sentences.chinese: 劳拉·克拉克为BBC资本撰文称，我们当中不太准时的人往往有一些共同的特点，比如“乐观、自我控制能力低、焦虑，或者喜欢寻求刺激”。

sentences.chinese: 你可能会问，为什么是乐观呢？

sentences.chinese: 乐观主义者往往会高估自己能完成的事情，低估问题——这意味着他们没有考虑到在来和你赴咖啡之约的路上会遇到长时间的交通堵塞。

sentences.english: Here’s another thought: maybe language is to blame?
sentences.chinese: 还有另一个想法：也许该怪语言？

sentences.english: The English phrase ‘to be fashionably late‘ is used to describe the optimum time to arrive at an event.
sentences.chinese: 英语短语“to be fashionably late”（时髦地迟到）被用来描述参加一个活动的最佳到达时间。

sentences.chinese: 如果你来得太早，你可能会显得过于急切，但如果你稍微晚一点，你似乎会显得很酷、很有品位。

sentences.english: The problem is, what one person regards as fashionably late, another may view as plain impolite.
sentences.chinese: 问题是，一个人认为的时髦地迟到，另一个人可能会认为是完全不礼貌的。

sentences.english: So, next time you have coffee, do try to be on time.
sentences.chinese: 所以，下次你去喝咖啡的时候，一定要尽量准时。
